title: Parental care and bird embryonic metabolism: A comparison between uniparentally incubating Silver‐throated Tits and biparentally incubating Black‐throated Tits
content:
Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog.


Abstract

Studies have shown that organisms may adjust metabolic rates in response to thermal variability, highlighting metabolic plasticity as a key adaptive mechanism. Understanding the extent of metabolic plasticity of an organism is key to predicting its adaptation to climate change. In birds, the embryos from the uniparentally incubating species are more frequently exposed to intermittent cooling due to the parents' repeated absences from the nest than the embryos from the species with biparental incubation. Such pressure may favour them to evolve a better ability to cope with the physiologically suppressive effects of low temperatures and temperature fluctuations. We compared embryonic heart rate, a proxy for embryonic metabolic rate, and its response to egg temperature change between two closely related species, the biparentally incubating Black-throated Tit (Aegithalos concinnus) and the uniparentally incubating Silver-throated Tit (Aegithalos glaucogularis). We also conducted an interspecific egg-swapping experiment to investigate the effect of incubation environment on embryonic metabolism and its consequences (i.e. incubation period length and hatching success). Consistent with the expectation, Silver-throated Tit exhibited a trend (although nonsignificant) of higher embryonic heart rate than Black-throated Tit. Also, when egg temperatures dropped, Silver-throated Tit showed a significantly slower decrease in embryonic heart rate than Black-throated Tit, suggesting that they may better cope with temperature drop. In the egg-swapping experiment, embryonic heart rates did not differ significantly between fostered and not-fostered eggs, but following fostering, heart rates tended to decrease in Silver-throated Tit embryos and increase in Black-throated Tit embryos, suggesting that embryos of both species show some responsiveness to new thermal environments. Egg-fostering treatment did not affect hatching success in either species, but the fostered eggs of Silver-throated Tits and Black-throated Tits tended to shorten and lengthen their incubation period, respectively, implying that the relatively stable biparental incubation environment may facilitate faster embryonic development than the more variable uniparental incubation environment. The findings enhance our understanding of the developmental strategies and responsiveness to changed environments in avian embryos under different parental care modes and provide insights into their potential to respond to climate change.

摘要

生物会通过调整代谢率来响应温度变化，这凸显了代谢可塑性作为一种重要适应机制的作用。了解生物代谢可塑性的程度对预测其应对气候变化的能力至关重要。在鸟类中，单亲孵卵物种由于亲鸟需频繁离巢，其胚胎比双亲孵卵物种更易经历间歇性降温。这种波动的温度环境可能使胚胎演化出更高的代谢率和更强的代谢可塑性，以更好地应对低温及温度波动对生理机能的抑制作用。 本研究比较了双亲孵卵的红头长尾山雀(Aegithalos concinnus)和单亲孵卵的银喉长尾山雀(Aegithalos glaucogularis)的胚胎心率(反映胚胎代谢率的指标)及其对卵温变化的响应，并通过种间换卵孵化实验，探究了孵化环境变化对胚胎代谢和孵卵期长度及孵化率的影响。 与预期一致，银喉长尾山雀胚胎的心率整体高于红头长尾山雀(但差异不显著)。当卵温下降时，银喉长尾山雀胚胎心率下降速度显著慢于红头长尾山雀，表明其可能更能耐受低温。在种间交换孵卵实验中，由异种代孵的卵与对照组未由异种代孵的卵的心率差异不显著，但由异种代孵的银喉长尾山雀卵的胚胎心率有下降趋势，而由异种代孵的红头长尾山雀卵的胚胎心率有上升趋势，说明二者对发育热环境变化皆具有一定响应能力。 种间交换孵卵实验不影响两个物种的孵化率，但由异种代孵的卵的孵化期在银喉长尾山雀中呈缩短趋势，而在红头长尾山雀中呈延长趋势。这表明相对稳定的双亲孵卵环境可能有利于加快胚胎发育，而温度波动更大的单亲孵卵环境可能导致发育延缓。 本研究增进了对不同亲代抚育模式下鸟类胚胎发育策略及其对环境变化响应能力的理解，并为评估其在气候变化背景下的适应能力提供参考。
